summary: DocuWave is a hybrid-SaaS report automation tool: a Go net/http API plus a Next.js app. A user connects their own data source (Postgres, MySQL, Google Sheets), its schema is introspected once and stored, and a report is saved as a structured query Spec + a template ID + a slot mapping + a list of output formats. Running a report always goes through report.Runner: compile the Spec against the stored schema, run it read-only, project the template's Doc, render PDF/XLSX/CSV in memory. Report queries are NOT written by an LLM any more — the llm package is retained but unwired from the report flow. Email delivery and scheduling from the PRD are not built yet.

tech_stack.framework: net/http with Go 1.22+ method+pattern routing (no web framework); Next.js 16 App Router + React 19 + Tailwind v4
tech_stack.database: PostgreSQL 17 via pgx/v5 pgxpool; embedded SQL migrations, no ORM
external_services: Google Sheets API v4 + Drive v3 + gviz query endpoint

key_conventions: Backend is one Go module (github.com/Max20050/docuwave) with feature packages under backend/internal/<domain>/. No shared 'models' or 'utils' package.
Within a package: store.go = pgx persistence, handlers.go = HTTP, plus domain files. writeJSON/writeError helpers are duplicated per package on purpose (unexported, package-local).
Every route is registered in one place: backend/cmd/api/main.go. Dependencies are constructed there and injected; there is no DI container or global state.
Protected routes are wrapped as authHandlers.RequireAuth(h.Method); the handler reads the caller via auth.UserIDFromContext(r.Context()).
Multi-tenancy is enforced in SQL: every store query filters `WHERE user_id = $n`. There is no row-level security or middleware substitute.
Sentinel errors are exported per package (ErrNotFound, ErrInvalidSpec, ErrUnknownTemplate...) and mapped to HTTP status in a writeXError helper in handlers.go. Use errors.Is, never string matching.

Secrets at rest are AES-256-GCM sealed with a nonce prefix, keyed by a base64 32-byte env var. Two independent keys/encryptors exist: DATASOURCE_ENCRYPTION_KEY (datasource.Encryptor) and LLM_ENCRYPTION_KEY (llm.Encryptor).
Migrations are numbered SQL files in backend/internal/migrate/migrations/, go:embed'd and run automatically at startup in filename order. Add the next NNNN_ file; never edit an applied one.

Pluggable layers are map/slice registries: datasource.connectorRegistry, llm.providerRegistry, render.renderers, template.Registry. Adding a variant = new file + one registry entry, no pipeline change.
Comments explain WHY, not what. The existing code is densely commented in that style — match it.

Frontend: pages are app/<route>/page.tsx, shared components are app/ui/<kebab-case>.tsx, and ALL backend calls go through frontend/lib/api.ts (typed wrapper + ApiError). Auth token lives in localStorage via lib/auth-context.tsx.
Tests are Go table-driven _test.go files next to the code. There are no frontend tests; CI runs go test, eslint, tsc --noEmit, and docker compose build.
notable_gaps: frontend/lib/api.ts and app/ui/report-builder.tsx are OUT OF SYNC with the backend: they still POST a `query` string and call POST /api/reports/generate-query, which main.go no longer registers. The backend now expects a structured `querySpec`. Report creation from the UI is broken until the frontend is ported to the Spec builder.
MVP items from the PRD that do not exist yet: email delivery, scheduling (fixed interval + manual trigger), and a report update/edit endpoint.
backend/internal/query/query.go references documents/v1/query-building.md, which is not in the repo.
frontend/app/page.tsx is still the create-next-app template, and layout.tsx metadata still says 'Create Next App'.
backend/api.exe is a committed build artifact.
